name.description:
The name of the package. It consists of vendor name and project name, separated by `/`.

Examples:

monolog/monolog
igorw/event-source
Required for published packages (libraries).

The name must be lowercase and consist of words separated by `-`, `.` or `_`. Before Composer 2.0, a name could contain any character.

type.description: Package types are used for custom installation logic. If you have a package that needs some special logic, you can define a custom type. This could be a `symfony-bundle`, a `wordpress-plugin` or a `typo3-module`. These types will all be specific to certain projects, and they will need to provide an installer capable of installing packages of that type.

target-dir.description:
Defines the installation target.

In case the package root is below the namespace declaration you cannot autoload properly. target-dir solves this problem.

An example is Symfony. There are individual packages for the components. The Yaml component is under `Symfony\Component\Yaml`. The package root is that Yaml directory. To make autoloading possible, we need to make sure that it is not installed into `vendor/symfony/yaml`, but instead into `vendor/symfony/yaml/Symfony/Component/Yaml`, so that the autoloader can load it from `vendor/symfony/yaml`.

"Deprecated in favor of PSR-4: only present to support legacy PSR-0 style autoloading. Not scheduled for removal, but all new code should preferably use PSR-4 without target-dir."

description.description:
A short description of the package. Usually this is just one line long.

Required for published packages (libraries).

readme.description:
A relative path to the readme document. Defaults to `README.md`.

Mainly useful for packages not on GitHub, as for GitHub packages Packagist.org will use the readme API to fetch the one detected by GitHub.

items.description: A tag/keyword that this package relates to.

keywords.description:
An array of keywords that the package is related to. These can be used for searching and filtering.

The special keywords `dev`, `testing` and `static analysis` make `composer require` prompt users to add the package to `require-dev` instead of `require`. Only unicode letters or numbers, space, dot, underscore and dash are allowed.

homepage.description: An URL to the website of the project.

version.description:
This must follow the format of `X.Y.Z` or `vX.Y.Z` with an optional suffix of `-dev`, `-patch` (`-p`), `-alpha` (`-a`), `-beta` (`-b`) or `-RC`. The patch, alpha, beta and RC suffixes can also be followed by a number.

Examples:

```
1.0.0
1.0.2
1.1.0
0.2.5
1.0.0-dev
1.0.0-alpha3
1.0.0-beta2
1.0.0-RC5
v2.0.4-p1
```
Optional if the package repository can infer the version from somewhere, such as the VCS tag name in the VCS repository. In that case it is also recommended to omit it.

time.description:
Release date of the version.
Must be in `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` format in UTC timezone.

license.description:
The license of the package. This can be either a string or an array of strings.
The recommended notation for the most common licenses is (alphabetical):
`Apache-2.0BSD-2-ClauseBSD-3-ClauseBSD-4-ClauseGPL-2.0-only / GPL-2.0-or-laterGPL-3.0-only / GPL-3.0-or-laterLGPL-2.1-only / LGPL-2.1-or-laterLGPL-3.0-only / LGPL-3.0-or-laterMIT`
For closed-source software, you may use `proprietary` as the license identifier.

authors.description: The authors of the package. This is an array of objects.

name.description: The author's name. Usually his real name.

homepage.description: An URL to the author's website.

role.description: The authors' role in the project (e.g. developer or translator)

funding.description:
A list of URLs to provide funding to the package authors for maintenance and development of new functionality.
Each entry consists of `type` (the platform, e.g. patreon, opencollective, tidelift or github) and `url`.

type.description: The type of funding, or the platform through which funding can be provided, e.g. patreon, opencollective, tidelift or github.

url.description: URL to a website with details, and a way to fund the package.

require.description:
Lists packages required by this package. The package will not be installed unless those requirements can be met.
It take an object which maps package names to [version constraints](https://getcomposer.org/doc/01-basic-usage.md#package-versions).
`require` and `require-dev` additionally support stability flags (root-only). These allow you to further restrict or expand the stability of a package beyond the scope of the [minimum-stability](http://getcomposer.org/doc/#minimum-stability) setting. You can apply them to a constraint, or just apply them to an empty constraint if you want to allow unstable packages of a dependency's dependency for example.
`require` and `require-dev` additionally support explicit references (i.e. commit) for dev versions to make sure they are blocked to a given state, even when you run update. These only work if you explicitly require a dev version and append the reference with `#`.

Examples:

```
"vendor/package":  "1.3.2",
// exactly 1.3.2
"vendor/package":  ">=1.3.2",
// anything above or equal to 1.3.2
"vendor/package":  "=1.3.0 =1.3.2 =1.3.0 =1.3.2 =0.3.2 , =, \<= specify upper / lower bounds
* wildcard
~ allows last digit specified to go up
^ doesn't allow breaking changes
```

"The `dev-master#` explicit references are discouraged and not actively supported: the package metadata is read from the branch, not the pinned commit. Only use as a temporary fix during development; prefer tagged releases."

replace.description:
Lists packages that are replaced by this package. This allows you to fork a package, publish it under a different name with its own version numbers, while packages requiring the original package continue to work with your fork because it replaces the original package.

This is also useful for packages that contain sub-packages, for example the main symfony/symfony package contains all the Symfony Components which are also available as individual packages. If you require the main package it will automatically fulfill any requirement of one of the individual components, since it replaces them.

Caution is advised when using replace for the sub-package purpose explained above. You should then typically only replace using `self.version` as a version constraint, to make sure the main package only replaces the sub-packages of that exact version, and not any other version, which would be incorrect.

conflict.description:
Lists packages that conflict with this version of this package. They will not be allowed to be installed together with your package.

Note: when specifying ranges like `=1.1`, this conflicts with all versions that are less than 1.0 *and* equal or newer than 1.1 at the same time — you probably want `=1.1` instead.

provide.description:
List of other packages that are provided by this package. This is mostly useful for implementations of common interfaces. A package could depend on some virtual package e.g. `psr/log-implementation`, any library that implements this interface would simply list it in `provide`.

Using `provide` with the name of an actual package rather than a virtual one implies that the code of that package is also shipped, in which case `replace` is generally a better choice.

require-dev.description:
Lists packages required for developing this package, or running tests, etc. (root-only).

The dev requirements of the root package are installed by default. Both `install` and `update` support the `--no-dev` option that prevents dev dependencies from being installed.
Packages listed here and their dependencies can not overrule the resolution found with the packages listed in require. If you run into such a conflict, you can specify the conflicting package in the require section and require the right version number to resolve the conflict.

Examples:

```
"vendor/package":  "1.3.2",
// exactly 1.3.2
"vendor/package":  ">=1.3.2",
// anything above or equal to 1.3.2
"vendor/package":  "=1.3.0 =1.3.2 =1.3.0 =1.3.2 =0.3.2 , =, \<= specify upper / lower bounds
* wildcard
~ allows last digit specified to go up
^ doesn't allow breaking changes
```

suggest.description:
Suggested packages that can enhance or work well with this package. These are just informational and are displayed after the package is installed, to give your users a hint that they could add more packages, even though they are not strictly required.
The format is like package links above, except that the values are free text and not version constraints.

config.description: A set of configuration options. It is only used for projects.

process-timeout.description: The timeout in seconds for process executions, defaults to 300 (5mins).

allow-plugins.description: Defaults to `{}`. As of Composer 2.2.0, allows you to restrict which Composer plugins are able to execute code during a Composer run. Set it to an object with package name patterns as keys, values being `true` to allow and `false` to disallow while suppressing further warnings and prompts. You can also set it to `false` to disallow all plugins, or `true` to allow all (NOT recommended).

use-include-path.description: If true, the Composer autoloader will also look for classes in the PHP include path.

use-parent-dir.description: When running Composer in a directory where there is no composer.json, if there is one present in a directory above, Composer will by default ask whether to use it instead. One of: true (always use parent if needed), false (never ask or use it) or "prompt" (ask every time), defaults to prompt.

preferred-install.description: Can be any of `source`, `dist` or `auto`. This option allows you to set the install method Composer will prefer to use.

source-fallback.description: DEPRECATED: will be removed in Composer 2.11. Defaults to false. If true, Composer will fall back to a different installation source (e.g. from dist to source) when a download fails. Automatic source fallback has security implications; do not set it unless you absolutely need it.

policy.description: Unified security and package policy configuration (security advisories, abandoned packages, malware, and custom policies). Set to false to disable all policy enforcement. Supersedes the deprecated audit.* options.

secure-http.description: Defaults to true. If set to true only HTTPS URLs are allowed to be downloaded via Composer. If you really absolutely need HTTP access to something then you can disable it, but using Let's Encrypt to get a free SSL certificate is generally a better alternative.

secure-svn-domains.description: Defaults to []. Lists domains which should be trusted/marked as using a secure Subversion/SVN transport. By default the svn:// protocol is seen as insecure and will throw. A better/safer alternative to disabling secure-http altogether.

bearer.description: A hash of domain name => bearer authentication tokens, for example {"example.org": "foo"} to authenticate using an "Authorization: Bearer foo" header.

bitbucket-oauth.description: A hash of domain name => consumers, typically {"bitbucket.org": {"consumer-key": "myKey", "consumer-secret": "mySecret"}}.

gitlab-token.description: A hash of domain name => private tokens, typically {"gitlab.com": "privatetoken"}, or an object with username and token keys for deploy tokens. The token must have api or read_api scope.

gitlab-protocol.description: A protocol to force when creating a repository URL for the source value of the package metadata. One of git or http (https is treated as a synonym for http). By default Composer generates a git-over-SSH URL for private repositories and HTTP(S) only for public.

forgejo-domains.description: A list of domains to use in forgejo mode. This is used for custom Forgejo setups, defaults to ["codeberg.org"].

forgejo-token.description: A list of domain names and username/access-tokens to authenticate against Forgejo servers, typically {"codeberg.org": {"username": "<user>", "token": "<access-token>"}}.

client-certificate.description: An object of domain name => {"local_cert": "...", "local_pk"?: "...", "passphrase"?: "..."} to provide a client certificate.

custom-headers.description: Custom HTTP headers for specific domains.

notify-on-install.description: Composer allows repositories to define a notification URL, so that they get notified whenever a package from that repository is installed. This option allows you to disable that behaviour.

github-protocols.description: A list of protocols to use for github.com clones, in priority order.

github-oauth.description: A list of domain names and oauth keys. Oauthtoken is used to access private repositories on github and to circumvent the low IP-based rate limiting of their API.

gitlab-oauth.description: A list of domain names and oauth keys. Oauthtoken is used to access private repositories on gitlab.

disable-tls.description: If set to true all HTTPS URLs will be tried with HTTP instead and no network level encryption is performed. Enabling this is a security risk and is NOT recommended. The better way is to enable the php_openssl extension in php.ini.

cafile.description: Location of Certificate Authority file on local filesystem. In PHP 5.6+ you should rather set this via openssl.cafile in php.ini, although PHP 5.6+ should be able to detect your system CA file automatically.

capath.description: If cafile is not specified or if the certificate is not found there, the directory pointed to by capath is searched for a suitable certificate. capath must be a correctly hashed certificate directory.

store-auths.description: What to do after prompting for authentication, one of: true (store), false (do not store) or "prompt" (ask every time), defaults to prompt.

platform.description: Lets you fake platform packages (PHP and extensions) so that you can emulate a production env or define your target platform in the config.

platform-check.description: Defaults to "php-only" which only checks the PHP version. Set to true to also check the presence of required PHP extensions. If set to false, Composer will not create and require a platform_check.php file as part of the autoloader bootstrap.

vendor-dir.description: The location where all packages are installed.

bin-dir.description: The location where all binaries are linked.

data-dir.description: Defaults to `C:UsersUserAppDataRoamingComposer` on Windows, $XDG_DATA_HOME/composer on unix systems that follow the XDG Base Directory Specifications, and $home on other unix systems. Right now it is only used for storing past composer.phar files to be able to rollback to older versions.

cache-dir.description: Stores all the caches used by composer. See also [COMPOSER_HOME](http://getcomposer.org/doc/03-cli.md#composer-home).

cache-files-dir.description: Stores the zip archives of packages.

cache-repo-dir.description: Stores repository metadata for the composer type and the VCS repos of type svn, github and bitbucket.

cache-vcs-dir.description: Stores VCS clones for loading VCS repository metadata for the git/hg types and to speed up installs.

cache-read-only.description: Defaults to false. Whether to use the Composer cache in read-only mode.

cache-ttl.description: The default cache time-to-live, defaults to 15552000 (6 months).

cache-files-ttl.description: Composer caches all dist (zip, tar, ...) packages that it downloads. Those are purged after six months of being unused by default. This option allows you to tweak this duration (in seconds) or disable it completely by setting it to 0.

cache-files-maxsize.description: Composer caches all dist (zip, tar, ...) packages that it downloads. When the garbage collection is periodically ran, this is the maximum size the cache will be able to use. Older (less used) files will be removed first until the cache fits.

bin-compat.description: Defaults to `auto`. Determines the compatibility of the binaries to be installed. If it is auto then Composer only installs .bat proxy files when on Windows. If set to `full` then both .bat files for Windows and scripts for Unix-based operating systems will be installed for each binary. This is mainly useful if you run Composer inside a linux VM but still want the .bat proxies available for use in the Windows host OS.

discard-changes.description: Can be any of `true`, `false` or `stash`. This option allows you to set the default style of handling dirty updates when in non-interactive mode. true will always discard changes in vendors, while `stash` will try to stash and reapply. Use this for CI servers or deploy scripts if you tend to have modified vendors.

autoloader-suffix.description: Optional string to be used as a suffix for the generated Composer autoloader. When null a random one will be generated.

optimize-autoloader.description: Always optimize when dumping the autoloader.

prepend-autoloader.description: If false, the composer autoloader will not be prepended to existing autoloaders, defaults to true.

classmap-authoritative.description: Defaults to false. If true, the Composer autoloader will only load classes from the classmap. Implies optimize-autoloader.

apcu-autoloader.description: Defaults to false. If true, the Composer autoloader will check for APCu and use it to cache found/not-found classes when the extension is enabled.

github-domains.description: A list of domains to use in github mode. This is used for GitHub Enterprise setups, defaults to ["github.com"].

github-expose-hostname.description: Defaults to true. If false, the OAuth tokens created to access the github API will have a date instead of the machine hostname.

gitlab-domains.description: A list of domains to use in gitlab mode.

archive-format.description: Defaults to tar. Composer allows you to add a default archive format when the workflow needs to create a dedicated archiving format.

archive-dir.description: Defaults to .. Composer allows you to add a default archive directory when the workflow needs to create a dedicated archiving format. Or for easier development between modules.

htaccess-protect.description: Defaults to true. If set to false, Composer will not create .htaccess files in the Composer home, cache, and data directories.

lock.description: Defaults to true. If set to false, Composer will not create a composer.lock file and will ignore it if one is present.

bump-after-update.description: Defaults to false and can be any of true, false, "dev" or "no-dev". If set to true, Composer will run the bump command after running the update command.

allow-missing-requirements.description: Defaults to false. If set to true, Composer will allow install when the lock file is not up to date with the latest changes in composer.json.

update-with-minimal-changes.description: Defaults to false. If set to true, Composer will only perform absolutely necessary changes to transitive dependencies during update.

sort-packages.description: Defaults to false. If true, the require command keeps packages sorted by name in `composer.json` when adding a new package.

extra.description:
Arbitrary extra data for consumption by `scripts`.
This can be virtually anything. To access it from within a script event handler, you can do:

```
$extra = $event->getComposer()->getPackage()->getExtra();
```

autoload.description:
Autoload mapping for a PHP autoloader.

Currently [PSR-4](http://www.php-fig.org/psr/psr-4/) autoloading, [PSR-0](https://github.com/php-fig/fig-standards/blob/master/accepted/PSR-0.md) autoloading, classmap generation and files are supported. PSR-4 is the recommended way though since it offers greater ease of use (no need to regenerate the autoloader when you add classes).

Under the `psr-4` key you define a mapping from namespaces to paths, relative to the package root. When autoloading a class like `Foo\Bar\Baz` a namespace prefix `Foo\` pointing to a directory `src/` means that the autoloader will look for a file named `src/Bar/Baz.php` and include it if present. Note that as opposed to the older PSR-0 style, the prefix (`Foo\`) is not present in the file path.

Under the `psr-0` key you define a mapping from namespaces to paths, relative to the package root. Note that this also supports the PEAR-style non-namespaced convention.

psr-0.description: This is a hash of namespaces (keys) and the directories they can be found into (values, can be arrays of paths) by the autoloader.

psr-4.description: This is a hash of namespaces (keys) and the PSR-4 directories they can map to (values, can be arrays of paths) by the autoloader.

classmap.description: This is an array of directories that contain classes to be included in the class-map generation process.

files.description: This is an array of files that are always required on every request.

exclude-from-classmap.description:
If you want to exclude some files or folders from the classmap you can use the `exclude-from-classmap` property. Useful to exclude test classes in your live environment, for example, as those will be skipped from the classmap even when building an optimized autoloader.

The paths are absolute from the package root directory, and support `*` to match anything but a slash, and `**` to match anything (`**` is implicitly added to the end of the paths).

autoload-dev.description: Same as "autoload", but only considered in development mode (root-only).

psr-0.description: This is a hash of namespaces (keys) and the directories they can be found into (values, can be arrays of paths) by the autoloader.

psr-4.description: This is a hash of namespaces (keys) and the PSR-4 directories they can map to (values, can be arrays of paths) by the autoloader.

classmap.description: This is an array of directories that contain classes to be included in the class-map generation process.

files.description: This is an array of files that are always required on every request.

archive.description:
Options for creating package archives.
The example will include `/dir/foo/bar/file`, `/foo/bar/baz`, `/file.php`, `/foo/my.test` but it will exclude `/foo/bar/any`, `/foo/baz`, and `/my.test`.

name.description: Allows configuring base name for archive. By default (if not configured, and `--file` is not passed as command-line argument), `preg_replace('#[^a-z0-9-_]#i', '-', name)` is used.

exclude.description: Allows configuring a list of patterns for excluded paths. The pattern syntax matches .gitignore files. A leading exclamation mark (!) will result in any matching files to be included even if a previous pattern excluded them, a leading slash will only match at the beginning of the project relative path and an asterisk will not expand to a directory separator.

repositories.description:
Custom package repositories to use (root-only: repository declarations of dependencies are ignored).
By default composer just uses the packagist repository. By specifying repositories you can get packages from elsewhere. Order is significant: Composer looks from the first to the last repository and picks the first match.

"The `pear` repository type was removed in Composer 2.0. The object (key/value) notation for repositories is deprecated in favor of the array notation, which now also supports a `name` property per repository."

- **composer** — The main repository type is the `composer` repository. It uses a single `packages.json` file that contains all of the package metadata. This is also the repository type that packagist uses. To reference a `composer` repository, just supply the path before the `packages.json` file. In case of packagist, that file is located at `/packages.json`, so the URL of the repository would be `repo.packagist.org`. For `example.org/packages.json` the repository URL would be `example.org`. See the [full documentation](http://getcomposer.org/doc/05-repositories.md#composer).

- **vcs** — VCS stands for version control system. This includes versioning systems like git, svn or hg. Composer has a repository type for installing packages from these systems. See the [full documentation](http://getcomposer.org/doc/05-repositories.md#vcs).

- **package** — If you want to use a project that does not support composer through any of the means above, you still can define the package yourself by using a `package` repository. Basically, you define the same information that is included in the `composer` repository's `packages.json`, but only for a single package. Again, the minimum required fields are `name`, `version`, and either of `dist` or `source`. See the [full documentation](http://getcomposer.org/doc/05-repositories.md#package).

- **artifact** — There are some cases, when there is no ability to have one of the previously mentioned repository types online, even the VCS one. Typical example could be cross-organisation library exchange through built artifacts. Of course, most of the times they are private. To simplify maintenance, one can simply use a repository of type `artifact` with a folder containing ZIP archives of those private packages. See the [full documentation](http://getcomposer.org/doc/05-repositories.md#artifact).

- **path** — In addition to the artifact repository, you can use the path one, which allows you to depend on a relative directory. This can be especially useful when dealing with monolith repositories. See the [full documentation](http://getcomposer.org/doc/05-repositories.md#path).

- **disabling packagist.org** — You can disable the default Packagist.org repository by adding this to your `composer.json`. See the [full documentation](https://getcomposer.org/doc/05-repositories.md#disabling-packagist-org).

items.description: A custom package repository definition. The `type` key selects the repository type.

type.description: Repository type: `composer` (packagist-like metadata), `vcs` (git/svn/hg), `package` (inline package definition), `artifact` (folder of zips) or `path` (local directory). See the `repositories` documentation for details on each type.

url.description: URL or path of the repository. The meaning depends on the repository type (e.g. the host serving `packages.json` for `composer`, a VCS URL for `vcs`, a directory of zips for `artifact`, a relative directory for `path`).

packagist.org.description: Set to `false` to disable the default packagist.org repository.

minimum-stability.description:
This defines the default behavior for filtering packages by stability. This defaults to `stable`, so if you rely on a `dev` package, you should specify it in your file to avoid surprises.
All versions of each package are checked for stability, and those that are less stable than the `minimum-stability` setting will be ignored when resolving your project dependencies. Specific changes to the stability requirements of a given package can be done in `require` or `require-dev`.Available options are `dev`, `alpha`, `beta`, `RC`, and `stable` (root-only).

prefer-stable.description: When this is enabled, Composer will prefer more stable packages over unstable ones when finding compatible stable packages is possible. If you require a dev version or only alphas are available for a package, those will still be selected granted that the minimum-stability allows for it (root-only).

bin.description: A set of files that should be treated as binaries and symlinked into the `bin-dir` (from config).

include-path.description: DEPRECATED: A list of directories which should get added to PHP's include path. This is only present to support legacy projects, and all new code should preferably use autoloading.
include-path.deprecated: Deprecated: only present to support legacy projects, prefer autoloading; no removal scheduled.

scripts.description:
Composer allows you to hook into various parts of the installation process through the use of scripts.
A script is a callback (defined as a static method) or a shell command that will be called when the event it listens on is triggered.
 Let's take a look to the full list of [Event Types](http://getcomposer.org/doc/articles/scripts.md#event-types).

`scripts` is a root-only field. Custom scripts can also get descriptions via `scripts-descriptions` and aliases via `scripts-aliases`.

pre-install-cmd.description: Occurs before the install command is executed, contains one or more Class::method callables or shell commands.

post-install-cmd.description: Occurs after the install command is executed, contains one or more Class::method callables or shell commands.

pre-update-cmd.description: Occurs before the update command is executed, contains one or more Class::method callables or shell commands.

post-update-cmd.description: Occurs after the update command is executed, contains one or more Class::method callables or shell commands.

pre-status-cmd.description: Occurs before the status command is executed, contains one or more Class::method callables or shell commands.

post-status-cmd.description: Occurs after the status command is executed, contains one or more Class::method callables or shell commands.

pre-package-install.description: Occurs before a package is installed, contains one or more Class::method callables or shell commands.

post-package-install.description: Occurs after a package is installed, contains one or more Class::method callables or shell commands.

pre-package-update.description: Occurs before a package is updated, contains one or more Class::method callables or shell commands.

post-package-update.description: Occurs after a package is updated, contains one or more Class::method callables or shell commands.

pre-package-uninstall.description: Occurs before a package has been uninstalled, contains one or more Class::method callables or shell commands.

post-package-uninstall.description: Occurs after a package has been uninstalled, contains one or more Class::method callables or shell commands.

pre-autoload-dump.description: Occurs before the autoloader is dumped, contains one or more Class::method callables or shell commands.

post-autoload-dump.description: Occurs after the autoloader is dumped, contains one or more Class::method callables or shell commands.

post-root-package-install.description: Occurs after the root-package is installed, contains one or more Class::method callables or shell commands.

post-create-project-cmd.description: Occurs after the create-project command is executed, contains one or more Class::method callables or shell commands.

scripts-descriptions.description: Descriptions for the custom commands defined in `scripts`, shown by `composer list` and `composer run -l` instead of the default "Runs the ... script as defined in composer.json".

scripts-aliases.description: Alternate names for the custom commands defined in `scripts`, as an array of strings per script. Available as of Composer 2.7.

php-ext.description: Settings for a PHP extension package, read by PIE (https://github.com/php/pie) rather than by Composer itself. Can only be set by packages whose type is php-ext or php-ext-zend.

irc.description: IRC channel for support, as irc://server/channel.

source.description: URL to browse or download the sources.

security.description: URL to the vulnerability disclosure policy (VDP).

support.description: Various information to get support about the project.

non-feature-branches.description: A set of string or regex patterns for non-numeric branch names that will not be handled as feature branches.

abandoned.description: Indicates whether this package has been abandoned, it can be boolean or a package name/URL pointing to a recommended alternative. Defaults to false.

_comment.description: Top level key used as a place to store comments (it can be a string or array of strings).
